identity.name: UUID-String Shellcode Staging with Enum-Callback Fileless Execution — Cortex ABIOC (Bookworm / ToneShell)
identity.summary: A DLL-sideloaded loader rebuilds shellcode from UUID strings via UuidFromStringA, copies it into a private executable heap, and runs it by passing the heap pointer as the callback to a Win32 enumeration API (EnumSystemLocalesA). No VirtualAlloc(RWX), no CreateThread, no injection — behavioral analytics catch the causality chain, not a signature.
identity.description: Unit 42 documented this fileless shellcode-staging technique across the Stately Taurus (Mustang Panda) ToneShell backdoor and the Bookworm malware family, using it as an attribution bridge: both families share the same UUID-string loader idiom and even a shared PDB dev-tree path (C:\Users\hack\Documents\WhiteFile\LTDIS13n\Release\LTDIS13n.pdb) across samples compiled eight weeks apart (ToneShell Sep 1 2022, Bookworm Oct 26 2022). Unit 42 states the loader is delivered by DLL side-loading (the report labels this T1574.001 under the legacy id; this card uses the MITRE-canonical T1574.002 for DLL Side-Loading) — a legitimately signed host application is planted alongside a malicious DLL in a user-writable directory so the trusted process loads attacker code. The report says only that the malware then decodes ASCII or Base64-encoded UUIDs into binary data and executes it via legitimate API functions; it does not name the specific APIs and does not attribute any callback API to a named sample. This card MODELS the well-known public form of that UUID-string technique: the payload is embedded as UUID strings, reassembled to raw bytes with UuidFromStringA, staged on a private executable heap (HeapCreate/HeapAlloc), and run by passing the buffer as the callback argument to a Win32 enumeration API such as EnumSystemLocalesA, EnumChildWindows, or EnumSystemLanguageGroupsA — an API idiom drawn from the public technique write-ups, not from the Unit 42 report. Because there is no RWX VirtualAlloc, no thread creation, and no remote injection, a BIOC keyed on those primitives sees nothing. The detection lever is behavioral: Cortex's auto-tuned ABIOCs learn that a given signed application never side-loads an unsigned DLL from a writable path and never loads an unsigned, unbacked (no on-disk image) module into itself. Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes (the side-load stage and the fileless unbacked-module execution), validation/hunt XQL surfaces each in xdr_data, and a correlation rule stitches them into one UUID-string-staging intrusion incident anchored to the signed-host-binary causality chain. T1620 (Reflective Code Loading) here is an analyst characterization of the in-memory execution, not a Unit 42-cited id. advanced-wildfire independently detonates the side-loaded loader and returns a malware verdict flagging the UUID-shellcode idiom.

campaigns: Stately Taurus espionage operations against government and NGO targets (2022-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-013 — Fileless UUID-string shellcode staging with enum-callback execution, modeled non-destructively for Cortex ABIOC validation.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM Windows agent installed with Behavioral Threat Protection / in-memory protection enabled so module-load and unbacked-execution telemetry reaches xdr_data.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE model of the UUID-string shellcode staging chain. No shellcode
# is ever made executable or run; every stage writes a SAFE-MODE marker so the
# telemetry shape (side-load path, UUID reassembly, enum-callback transfer) is
# present for Cortex to reason over without any real payload.
$stage = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'cortexsim-edr-013'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $stage | Out-Null
# (1) DLL side-load staged from a user-writable path
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $stage 'SAFE-MODE-sideloaded-module.dll.marker') -Value 'CortexSim SIM-EDR-013 SAFE-MODE marker: models an unsigned DLL side-loaded from a user-writable path into a signed host process. No executable code is present.'
# (2) UUID-string reassembly modeled with benign, inert UUIDs (real [guid] parse, never executed)
$uuids = @('00010203-0405-0607-0809-0a0b0c0d0e0f','10111213-1415-1617-1819-1a1b1c1d1e1f')
$bytes = foreach ($u in $uuids) { ([guid]$u).ToByteArray() }
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $stage 'SAFE-MODE-decoded-blob.marker') -Value ("CortexSim SIM-EDR-013 SAFE-MODE: reassembled {0} inert bytes from {1} benign UUID strings (models UuidFromStringA). Bytes are never placed on an executable heap and never run." -f $bytes.Count, $uuids.Count)
# (3) Enum-callback transfer modeled as a marker only (no heap made executable, no callback invoked)
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $stage 'SAFE-MODE-enum-callback-exec.marker') -Value 'CortexSim SIM-EDR-013 SAFE-MODE marker: models control transfer into a private executable heap via an EnumSystemLocalesA / EnumChildWindows callback. Telemetry-shape marker only.'
Write-Host 'cortexsim-edr-013-fileless-staging-chain-modeled'

expected_artifacts.description: A signed host application loads an unsigned DLL from a user-writable path (DLL side-loading) — the delivery stage of the loader.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: actor_process_signature_status = "SIGNED" and action_module_signature_status in ("UNSIGNED", "UNKNOWN") and action_module_path contains "\Users\"

expected_artifacts.description: A signed host process loads an unsigned, unbacked module (no on-disk image; action_module_path empty) into itself — the xdr_data footprint of the fileless UUID-string reflective load. The enum-callback (EnumSystemLocalesA) transfer is tradecraft context, not a queryable column. No VirtualAlloc(RWX), no CreateThread.
SAFE-MODE marker files written under %TEMP%\cortexsim-edr-013 modeling each stage of the chain (non-destructive).

cleanup.code: Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'cortexsim-edr-013') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[CortexSim] SIM-EDR-013 cleanup complete — SAFE-MODE markers removed.'

iocs.context: Compile-time PDB dev-tree path embedded in both ToneShell and Bookworm loader samples (compiled eight weeks apart) — the shared-development attribution artifact Unit 42 used to bridge the two families. A hunt/YARA indicator, not a runtime IOC.

abiocs.name: EDR-013 DLL Side-Loaded Module Loads from a User-Writable Path in a Signed Host Process
abiocs.description: Cortex's learned per-application baseline is that a given signed host binary installed under Program Files / System32 loads only its known, signed modules from its own install tree. The ABIOC fires on the baseline deviation where such a signed, trusted-path host binary loads an unsigned/unknown DLL from a user-writable path (Users, ProgramData, AppData, Temp) that differs from the host binary's install directory — the classic search-order-hijack shape of the UUID-string loader's side-load delivery stage. Constraining the actor to a Program Files / Windows install location suppresses the benign case of an AppData-resident app (Teams, Slack, updaters) loading its own unsigned components, so the anchor is the anomalous causality chain (trusted-path signed host binary -> unsigned module from a writable path outside its install tree), not any known-bad DLL name. Unit 42 labeled this side-loading T1574.001 under the legacy id; this card carries the MITRE-canonical T1574.002 (DLL Side-Loading).
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.MODULE and event_sub_type = ENUM.MODULE_LOAD
| filter actor_process_signature_status = "SIGNED"
| filter actor_process_image_path contains "\Program Files" or actor_process_image_path contains "\Windows\"
| filter action_module_signature_status in ("UNSIGNED", "UNKNOWN")
| filter action_module_path contains "\Users\" or action_module_path contains "\ProgramData\" or action_module_path contains "\AppData\" or action_module_path contains "\Temp\"
| comp count() as sideloaded_modules by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_path, actor_process_instance_id, action_module_name, action_module_path
| filter sideloaded_modules >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, action_module_name, action_module_path, sideloaded_modules
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-application module-load baseline (signed process loads only its signed modules from trusted paths) -> deviation: the signed host binary side-loads an unsigned/unknown DLL from a user-writable directory, anchored to the loading process. Surfaces causality_actor_process_image_name + actor_process_instance_id so the side-load stage shares the CGO / causality-actor join key with the fileless-execution ABIOC and CR-EDR-0013.

abiocs.name: EDR-013 Unbacked Private-Heap Execution Reached via Locale or Window Enumeration Callback
abiocs.description: The fileless core: a signed host process loads an unsigned module that has no backing image on disk (action_module_path is empty — an in-memory / unbacked region rather than a file-backed DLL) into its own address space. This is the observable xdr_data footprint of the UUID-string reflective-load idiom (bytes reassembled with UuidFromStringA onto a private heap and run without a file), which produces no VirtualAlloc(RWX), no CreateThread, and no cross-process injection to key on. In the public form of the technique control is handed to that region by passing it as the callback argument to a Win32 enumeration API such as EnumSystemLocalesA / EnumChildWindows / EnumSystemLanguageGroupsA — that callback idiom is tradecraft context, not a queryable xdr_data column, so the ABIOC anchors the deviation to the in-process causality (signed host process -> unsigned unbacked module load) that Cortex's behavioral-ML has never observed for that application. Sibling card TTP-2026-0119 keys the same unbacked-execution shape on action_module_path = "" + action_module_signature_status = "UNSIGNED".
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.MODULE and event_sub_type = ENUM.MODULE_LOAD
| filter causality_actor_process_signature_status = "SIGNED"
| filter action_module_path = "" and action_module_signature_status = "UNSIGNED"
| comp count() as unbacked_module_loads by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, action_module_signature_status
| filter unbacked_module_loads >= 1
| sort desc unbacked_module_loads
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, unbacked_module_loads
abiocs.causality_anchor: In-process causality: signed host process -> private executable heap region unbacked by any disk image -> control transfer via a locale/window enumeration callback, a lineage the learned per-application behavioral profile has never exhibited.

xql_queries.name: EDR-013 Unsigned DLL Side-Loaded from a User-Writable Path by a Signed Host Binary
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.MODULE and event_sub_type = ENUM.MODULE_LOAD
| filter actor_process_signature_status = "SIGNED"
| filter actor_process_image_path contains "\Program Files" or actor_process_image_path contains "\Windows\"
| filter action_module_signature_status in ("UNSIGNED", "UNKNOWN")
| filter action_module_path contains "\Users\" or action_module_path contains "\ProgramData\" or action_module_path contains "\AppData\" or action_module_path contains "\Temp\"
| comp count() as sideload_events by agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_module_name
| filter sideload_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_module_name, sideload_events

xql_queries.name: EDR-013 Fileless Unbacked Unsigned Module Loaded by a Signed Host Process
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.MODULE and event_sub_type = ENUM.MODULE_LOAD
| filter causality_actor_process_signature_status = "SIGNED"
| filter action_module_path = "" and action_module_signature_status = "UNSIGNED"
| comp count() as fileless_exec by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter fileless_exec >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, fileless_exec

correlation_rules.name: UUID-String Shellcode Staging with Enum-Callback Execution — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(EDR-013 DLL Side-Loaded Module Loads from a User-Writable Path in a Signed Host Process) AND ABIOC(EDR-013 Unbacked Private-Heap Execution Reached via Locale or Window Enumeration Callback) observed on the same agent_hostname and causality_actor_process_image_name (the shared CGO / causality-actor join key both ABIOCs now surface, with actor_process_instance_id / causality_actor_process_instance_id pinning the exact process nodes) within a 10-minute window — fuses the side-loading delivery stage and the fileless enum-callback shellcode execution into a single UUID-string-staging intrusion incident anchored to the signed-host-binary causality chain (no VirtualAlloc RWX, no CreateThread, no cross-process injection to key on).

use_cases.name: Fileless UUID-String Shellcode Staging Detection via Cortex Behavioral Analytics
use_cases.description: Prove that Cortex catches a fileless loader that reassembles shellcode from UUID strings and executes it through a Win32 enumeration callback — a chain that produces none of the classic RWX-allocation / thread-creation / injection primitives a static BIOC keys on. The catch comes from the auto-tuned ABIOCs anchoring the deviation to the signed-host-binary causality chain, with WildFire independently condemning the loader.

test_cases.objective: The DLL side-loading delivery stage is detected as a behavioral deviation from the signed application's learned module-load baseline.
preconditions: Windows endpoint with the Cortex agent installed and a learned per-application module-load baseline.
A signed host binary staged alongside an unsigned DLL in a user-writable path.
steps: Stage the signed host binary + unsigned side-load DLL in a user-writable directory.
Trigger the load and observe the side-load ABIOC fire.
Confirm the side-load validation XQL surfaces the unsigned module-load in xdr_data.
success_criteria: ABIOC `EDR-013 DLL Side-Loaded Module Loads from a User-Writable Path in a Signed Host Process` fires.
XQL `EDR-013 Unsigned DLL Side-Loaded from a User-Writable Path by a Signed Host Binary` returns the loading process + unsigned module.

test_cases.objective: The fileless enum-callback execution from an unbacked private heap is detected without any RWX allocation, thread creation, or injection signal.
preconditions: Windows endpoint with Behavioral Threat Protection / in-memory protection enabled so unbacked-execution telemetry reaches xdr_data.
steps: Reassemble shellcode from UUID strings into a private executable heap.
Transfer control via an EnumSystemLocalesA / EnumChildWindows callback.
Observe the fileless-execution ABIOC fire and the hunt XQL surface the unbacked enum-callback region.
success_criteria: ABIOC `EDR-013 Unbacked Private-Heap Execution Reached via Locale or Window Enumeration Callback` fires.
XQL `EDR-013 Fileless Enumeration-Callback Execution from an Unbacked Memory Region` returns the signed causality process + enum-callback API.

test_cases.objective: The two behavioral deviations are stitched into a single UUID-string-staging intrusion incident.
preconditions: Both ABIOCs have fired on the same host + causality process within the correlation window.
steps: Let the side-load and fileless-execution ABIOCs fire in sequence.
Observe CR-EDR-0013 raise one stitched incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EDR-0013` raises exactly one UUID-string-staging incident anchored to the signed-host-binary causality chain.

preventive_controls: Enforce DLL search-order hardening and signed-DLL policy (WDAC / AppLocker) so signed host applications cannot side-load unsigned modules from user-writable paths.
Enable Cortex XDR in-memory / Behavioral Threat Protection so execution from unbacked private-heap regions is blocked, not merely detected.
Deliver spear-phishing attachments through Advanced WildFire detonation so the side-loaded loader is condemned before it reaches the endpoint.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-application module-load and in-memory-execution baseline rather than hand-authoring signatures for individual RWX/CreateThread primitives that this technique deliberately avoids.
Alert on a signed process loading an unsigned/unknown DLL from a user-writable path.
Alert on execution reaching an unbacked private/heap region through a locale or window enumeration callback (EnumSystemLocalesA / EnumChildWindows / EnumSystemLanguageGroupsA).
